Was looking at the promos for villains tonight to think about how I would play the new promos and was looking at naturalist ability. Where you get to pick what form powers the naturist gets to use. So my question for a discussion will be how useful will the form cards be using this promo.

advantage: you have a lot of choices to do. So could be using advantages from both alligator and rhino forms powers.

Disadvantage: possibility of a dead card in your hand and have to spend on play phase to get that form card down. Also form cards have powers so you would have to project a turn in ahead if you want to use a different forms ability from one shots than the form you want. 

here is actually a question that would be good to get an official ruling on with this card. If I have a rhino form down and use the prey power to be able to use alligator form abilities from one shots, then in my next turn I can use both alligators and rhino form abilities on one shots. I play a one shot that has both forms on there like primal charge or the power on natural form power,technically since both forms are active, then nothing should stop you from activating both since it should resolve everything on the card when played. In the case of natural form since they are all listed under the same power then again all should resolve. Is this a correct assumption and the plan for this deck since this almost feels a bit overpowered for this deck. Or do we still only pick one of the 3 in this case?

posts.cooked: Fixed Point makes wonderful things possible.  Normally you can have only one form in play, because whenever a form enters play, all other forms are destroyed.  But Fixed Point prevents all cards from leaving play, so if you play or put into play his forms while FIxed Point is in play, you'll turn him into a gazhinodile.

The power level of the new promo depends on how soon you get a form, and how long you keep it in play.

If you take him into random matches the promo should be slightly less powerful, largely because you can't switch from +1 to -1 as the situation warrants.  Desperate Prey is a lot of fun, and a great promo.  It has a lot of strebgths, but you lose a lot and gain a lot.  It is a great promo.

I’m relatively new to them, but I think that’s the best kind of promo! I love it when the new power completely changes how you look at a deck, without that being obvious up front. (An example is Dark Visionary, with whom I’m much more likely to play her damage-dealing one-shots than her more Visionary-unique cards, because her power always gives her deck manipulation capability.)
